title: The company operating Obex's Liquidity Layer is Treadstone, which commits directly to a 90% Encumbrance Ratio ceiling
content:
A.6.1.1.5.2.6.1.2.1.3.1 states: "**Treadstone will operate the Obex Liquidity Layer** and agrees to stay at or below a 90% Encumbrance Ratio."

Treadstone was introduced far earlier in the Artifact as "the development company that provides services to Rubicon" (A.6.1.1.5.2.1.1.3.1.1.6), Rubicon being the Prime Foundation associated with Obex. The chain of relationships is therefore Obex → Rubicon → Treadstone, yet the operating responsibility and the leverage commitment attach at the far end of that chain.

Two consequences follow. First, the party actually moving capital is not the Agent and not the Foundation but a contracted supplier, which is why the TRC base-class inheritance clause (A.6.1.1.5.2.6.1.2.1.3.2) is drafted as binding *Treadstone* rather than Obex. Obligations follow the operator, not the owner.

Second, an undertaking of real financial significance — a hard leverage ceiling — is given by an entity that OBEX token holders do not appoint, cannot vote on, and have no direct contractual relationship with. Their recourse runs through the Foundation's contracting discretion, not through the Root Edit process.

The compensating control is that enforcement does not depend on the contract chain at all. The Freezer Multisig can halt the Liquidity Layer when "Obex is not complying with rules regarding Risk Capital or Asset Liability Management," and Soter Labs can reach that threshold alone. The commitment is contractual; the enforcement is a key.
description: The operator is the development company contracted to the Rubicon Foundation, so the leverage undertaking is given by a party two steps removed from Obex's token holder governance.
